'''Ian Macmillan Ward''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS|FInstP}} (9 April 1928 – 5 November 2018)<ref>[http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/thetimes-uk/obituary.aspx?n=ian-macmillan-ward&pid=190697711 Professor Ian Macmillan Ward]</ref> was a British physicist specialising in [[polymer science]]. He was Cavendish Professor of Physics in the School of Physics and Astronomy at the [[University of Leeds]] where he was also chairman of the School of Physics and Astronomy and first director of the [[Polymer Interdisciplinary Research Centre]].<ref name="FRS" /><ref name="Energy at Leeds">{{cite web | title=Professor Ian Ward | website=Energy at Leeds | url=http://www.energy.leeds.ac.uk/about-us/people/smart-grids/142/ | access-date=22 September 2017}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Ward was educated at the [[Royal Grammar School, Newcastle upon Tyne]] and [[Magdalen College, Oxford]].<ref name="whoswho" />

== Career ==
Ward joined the Fibres division of the [[Imperial Chemical Industries]] as technical officer in 1954. Following a [[secondment]] to the Division of Applied Mathematics of [[Brown University]] (1961–1962), he became the head of the Basic Physics Section at the company. In 1965, he joined the [[University of Leeds]] as a lecturer in physics of materials, becoming a professor of physics in 1970 and Cavendish Professor in 1989, before retiring in 1994.<ref name="whoswho" /><ref name="internationalwhoswho" /> He chaired the Department of Physics at Leeds from 1975 until 1978 and from 1987 until 1989.<ref name="whoswho" /><ref name="ETH Zurich 20162" /> He served as the president of the [[British Society of Rheology]] from 1984 until 1986.<ref name="whoswho" /> In 1989, he became the first director of the [[Polymer Interdisciplinary Research Centre]], holding the position until 1994.<ref name="whoswho" /><ref name="internationalwhoswho" />  Ward was also a visiting professor at the [[University of Bradford]].

He published 700 peer-reviewed journal articles, 6 textbooks and 20 major patents.<ref name="FRS" /> He served as Editor of the journal ''Polymer'' published by [[Elsevier]].<ref name="FRS" /><ref name="Celebrating the 50th Anniversary of Polymer">{{cite web | title=Journal History :: Celebrating the 50th Anniversary of Polymer :: The International Journal for the Science and Technology of Polymers | website=Celebrating the 50th Anniversary of Polymer | url=http://www.polymer50.com/journal-history/ | access-date=22 September 2017}}</ref> He was managing director of several University of Leeds [[University spin-off|spin-off companies]]. These include Vantage Polymers for single polymer self-reinforced [[Composite material|composites]], [[die (manufacturing)|die]]-[[drawing (manufacturing)|drawn]] ropes and tubes, and Leeds Lithium Power for thermoreversible, [[Ionic conductivity (solid state)|ionically conducting]] polymer [[gel]] [[electrolyte]]s used to manufacture [[lithium battery|lithium batteries]].<ref name="FRS" /><ref name="Energy at Leeds" />

== Awards and honours ==
Ward received awards from the [[Institute of Physics]]: Charles Vernon Boys Medal (1993), [[Glazebrook Medal]] (2004) – and the [[Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining|Institute of Materials]]: Griffith Medal (1982), Swinburne Medal (1988) and the Netlon Award (2004).<ref name="whoswho" /><ref name="FRS" /><ref name="Energy at Leeds" /> In 1993, he received an honorary doctorate from the University of Bradford.<ref name="internationalwhoswho" /><ref name="FRS" />

He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1983|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1983]].<ref name="FRS">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/ian-ward-12483|title=Ian Ward|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London}} One or more of the preceding sentences may incorporate text from the royalsociety.org website where "all text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License." {{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |access-date=9 March 2016 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170710134855/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archive-date=10 July 2017 }}, "Intellectual property rights"</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Coates |first=Philip David |date=2025 |title=Ian Macmillan Ward: 9 April 1928 — 5 November 2018 |url=https://doi.org/10.1098/rsbm.2024.0027 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=79}}</ref> His certificate of election reads: {{centered pull quote|Physicist.  Distinguished for his comprehensive investigations of properties of solid [[polymer]]s and their relation to structure. The main thread through his work has been the elucidation of mechanical behaviour in highly [[anisotropic]] systems. He established the comprehensive methodology for characterising such systems, involving a wide range of mechanical, [[spectroscopic]] and other structure techniques. Through these he established correlations between properties and structure which have greatly contributed to the understanding of the behaviour of these systems and to the achievement of desired properties by planned orientation procedures. In the latter respect his work has led to the attainment of ultraoriented [[Fiber#Human-made fibers|fibrous]] material of greatly enhanced [[stiffness]] and strength.  Professor Ward also made salient contributions to [[Viscoelasticity|viscoelastic]] [[Stress relaxation|relaxations]], [[nonlinearity|non-linear]] viscoelasticity, [[Yield (engineering)|yield]] behaviour and to the study of [[Chemical structure|molecular conformations]] by spectroscopic methods.<ref name="frsCitation">{{cite web|url=https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqCmd=Show.tcl&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqPos=0&dsqSearch=%28RefNo%3D%27EC%2F1983%2F37%27%29|title=EC/1983/37: Ward, Ian Macmillan|publisher=[[The Royal Society]]|access-date=21 September 2017}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>}}

The Ian Macmillan Ward Prize for the Best Student Publication, awarded every two years to PhD students by the Institute of Physics Polymer Physics Group, is named in his honour.<ref name="Physics">{{cite web | last=Physics | first=Institute of | title=Ian Macmillan Ward Prize for the Best Student Publication | website=Institute of Physics – For physics • For physicists • For all | url=http://www.iop.org/activity/groups/subject/pol/prize/publication/page_40831.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110309170610/http://www.iop.org/activity/groups/subject/pol/prize/publication/page_40831.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=9 March 2011 | access-date=22 September 2017 }}</ref><ref name="MaPS">{{cite web | author=MaPS | title=Ian Ward: School of Physics and Astronomy, University of Leeds | website=Home | url=http://www.physics.leeds.ac.uk/physics-at-leeds/our-physicists/ian-ward.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170925035955/http://www.physics.leeds.ac.uk/physics-at-leeds/our-physicists/ian-ward.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=25 September 2017 | access-date=22 September 2017 }}</ref>

In 2013, the Department of Materials of [[ETH Zurich]] awarded him the Staudinger–Durrer Prize ''in recognition of his pioneering contributions to the field of mechanical properties of solid polymers and polymer-based composites.''<ref name="FRS" /><ref name="Energy at Leeds" /><ref name="ETH Zurich 2016">{{cite web | title=Staudinger-Durrer Prize | website=ETH Zurich | date=15 January 2016 | url=https://www.mat.ethz.ch/department/staudinger-durrer-prize.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170925040220/https://www.mat.ethz.ch/department/staudinger-durrer-prize.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=25 September 2017 | access-date=22 September 2017 }}</ref><ref name="ETH Zurich 20162">{{cite web | title=Materials Day 2013 – Today, Tomorrow and Beyond | website=ETH Zurich | date=16 January 2016 | url=https://www.mat.ethz.ch/news-and-events/events/events-archive/materials-day/2013.html | access-date=24 September 2017}}</ref>
